final_message:
The bug was in `record_failure` in `billing/dunning.py`. When retries ran out and the dunning policy's `final_action` was `"cancel"`, the code had a stray `pass` where the invoice should have been marked uncollectible. It canceled the subscription but left the invoice `open`. I replaced the `pass` with `mark_uncollectible(ctx, invoice["id"])`.

All 25 tests pass, including the reproduction test.

I put that test in a new file, `tests/test_dunning_cancel.py`. I also wrote `answer.json` in the repository root with `{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}`.

I only changed the `"cancel"` branch. The `"pause"` and `"mark_unpaid"` branches also leave the invoice open, which looks intentional because the subscription can recover later.

steps.command: cd .. && sed -i '/^        pass$/c\        mark_uncollectible(ctx, invoice["id"])' billing/dunning.py && echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}' > answer.json && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cd .. && echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}' > answer.json && cat >> tests/test_dunning_cancel.py <<'EOF'


def test_cancel_policy_marks_uncollectible():
    from conftest import World

    w = World({"retry_offsets_days": [2], "final_action": "cancel"})
    cus = w.customer(last4="9995")
    sub = w.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(w.monthly["id"], 1)])
    w.advance_days(2)
    [inv] = w.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["status"] == "uncollectible"
    assert sub["status"] == "canceled"
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
